prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in Houston, Texas, and has neck strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1234; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement is about the collision you reported in Houston. Do you understand that this call is being recorded?

A: Yes, I understand.

Q: Please tell me in your own words what happened.

A: I was driving down the main road in the right lane. The other car came over into my lane while trying to pass a slower vehicle. I tapped the brakes and steered right, but we still met nose to nose. It wasn't a hard hit, but it was enough to jolt me.

Q: How fast were you going when the vehicles made contact?

A: I'd say maybe fifteen or twenty miles an hour. Traffic was moving slowly that afternoon.

Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt?

A: Yes, I was. The airbags didn't deploy, but the belt caught me hard.

Q: Did you get checked out by anyone after the collision?

A: I drove myself to an urgent care clinic later that evening. My neck was sore and stiff, and I had a headache that got worse overnight.

Q: Can you describe the neck symptoms you are experiencing now?

A: It's tight across the back and sides, and turning my head to the left hurts. Sitting at a desk for long stretches makes it worse. The doctor said it looks like a neck strain and gave me exercises and some medication.

Q: Have you had any neck problems or injuries before this collision?

A: Nothing serious. I had some stiffness now and then from sleeping wrong, but nothing that kept me from working.

Q: Is there anything else you would like to add to your statement?

A: No, I think that covers it. I'm still going to physical therapy twice a week, and I'll send you the records when I get them.

Q: Thank you. This concludes the statement.
